ZULMA LOPEZ.name: Zulma Lopez
ZULMA LOPEZ.background: Democrat from Atlanta (DeKalb County); born May 2, 1977 and raised in Puerto Rico. B.A., University of Puerto Rico (1999); J.D., University of Puerto Rico School of Law (2003). Moved to Georgia in 2007; immigration attorney who has owned Lopez Immigration LLC since 2014. Married to DeKalb County State Court Judge Dax López; four children. In 2020 challenged incumbent Rep. Served Jan. 11, 2021 to Jan. 9, 2023; announced Feb. 4, 2022 that she would not seek re-election; succeeded by Imani Barnes.
ZULMA LOPEZ.record: Served on the Economic Development and Tourism, Judiciary Non-Civil and Science and Technology committees (2021-2022). The House press office said she built enough credibility on Judiciary Non-Civil to influence bills and make them less restrictive, and she voted in 2021 to repeal the citizen's arrest law.
ZULMA LOPEZ.notes: Conflict: Wikipedia dates her runoff win as Aug. 20, 2020; Wikipedia spells the incumbent 'Michelle' in body text; correct is Michele Henson. Did not complete the 2020 Candidate Connection survey. The 'citizen's arrest' item is from the House press release, not a roll call; state votes/bills left to official records.

positions.stance: Said she would keep advocating for immigrant voices after leaving office, citing Georgia's roughly one million Latinos (about 10% of the population).
